title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion formed on the income statement; cash conversion and debt-to-fixed-asset discipline are facts audited on the balance sheet.
epigraph.author: Forensic accounting maxim

web_blocks.html: Over the six-year window from FY21 through FY26 (and TTM through September 2026), SEDEMAC delivered exceptional top-line and profit compounding: revenue grew from ₹240 Cr in FY21 to ₹1,058 Cr in FY26 (34.5% 5-year CAGR) and ₹1,265 Cr TTM, while Net Profit compounded from ₹7 Cr to ₹104 Cr in FY26 (69.4% 5-year profit CAGR) and ₹129 Cr TTM [1]. Operating margins expanded from 10–12% (FY21–FY23) to 20% in FY26 before moderating to 19% in Q1–Q2 FY27 on PCB and semiconductor inflation [1, 5].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Consolidated Profit & Loss Trajectory (Mar 2021 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue scaled 5.3x from FY21 (₹240 Cr) to TTM (₹1,265 Cr) with operating leverage lifting OPM from 10% (FY22) to 19–20% (FY26–TTM) [1].

web_blocks.html: The most urgent forensic item sits on the September 2026 (H1 FY27) Balance Sheet [1]. In six months from March 2026 to September 2026, Borrowings jumped nearly 5x from ₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr (+₹280 Cr) [1]. Over the same period, Fixed Assets more than doubled from ₹253 Cr to ₹518 Cr (+₹265 Cr), while CWIP moved from ₹91 Cr to ₹63 Cr and Other Assets rose from ₹470 Cr to ₹606 Cr [1]. Quarterly Interest expense jumped from ₹1–2 Cr to ₹6 Cr in Q2 FY27 [1]. Three simultaneous cash drains explain this surge. First was heavy capex and facility recognition for the 120,000 sq. ft. MF3 Chakan plant and MF5 Shoolagiri land [5]. Second, working capital expanded from ~₹135 Cr to ~₹258 Cr as SEDEMAC built chip inventory and shortened supplier payables [5]. Third, management funded both through internal accruals and debt rather than equity dilution [1, 5].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Consolidated Balance Sheet Forensics (Mar 2021 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sep 2026 Borrowings surged from ₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr and Fixed Assets from ₹253 Cr to ₹518 Cr to fund MF3/MF5 capex and semiconductor-driven working capital [1, 5].

web_blocks.html: A second forensic flag involves cash conversion, DSO stretch, and interest capitalization [1]. In FY26, Cash Flow from Operations (₹128 Cr) covered 123% of PAT (₹104 Cr) and 71% of pre-tax EBITDA. Yet Capital Expenditure of ₹175 Cr (-₹148 Cr net investing outflow) pushed Free Cash Flow to -₹47 Cr [1]. Debtor Days stretched from 24 days in FY25 (29.7 days prior baseline) to 46.1 days in FY26. Meanwhile, Days Payable jumped from 76 to 128 days in FY26 before reversing in H1 FY27 as management paid chip suppliers faster [1, 5]. Automated screening also flags potential interest capitalization on CWIP (₹53 Cr in FY25, ₹91 Cr in FY26, ₹63 Cr in Sep 2026). With borrowings now at ₹352 Cr, investors must verify Ind AS 23 capitalized borrowing costs in annual footnotes so true interest coverage is not overstated [1].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Conversion (Mar 2021 – Mar 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: FY26 CFO rose to ₹128 Cr (71% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA), but ₹175 Cr of growth capex produced -₹47 Cr Free Cash Flow [1].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Working Capital Cycle & Return Ratios (Mar 2021 – Mar 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE expanded steadily from 6% (FY22) to 35.3% (FY26), though Debtor Days stretched to 46 days and H1 FY27 debt/capex will test capital efficiency [1].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Checklist: Three Accounting & Cash Items to Monitor in FY27
paragraphs: 1. Borrowings & Lease Liabilities (₹72 Cr → ₹352 Cr): Monitor whether H1 FY27 debt peaks as MF3 transitions from pilot to commercial revenue, or climbs further as MF5 construction accelerates [1, 5].
2. Interest Capitalization & Q2 Interest Step-Up: Quarterly finance cost jumped to ₹6 Cr in Q2 FY27; verify how much interest on MF3/MF5 loans was capitalized to CWIP under Ind AS 23 [1].
3. Debtor Days (46.1 days) & Payables Reversal: If OEMs keep receivables near 45+ days while chip vendors demand shorter payables, working capital will remain a cash sink [1, 5].

book_paragraphs: Now let us open the forensic ledger and examine whether SEDEMAC's earnings are backed by clean cash and a fortress balance sheet—or whether rapid growth is starting to strain the plumbing. Look first at the six-year income statement: sales climbed from ₹240 crore in FY21 to ₹1,058 crore in FY26 and ₹1,265 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis, while net profit compounded at 69.4% annually over five years to ₹104 crore in FY26 and ₹129 crore TTM. Return on Capital Employed marched steadily higher from 6% in FY22 to 35.3% in FY26, with Return on Equity at 26.9%. On the surface, those are elite numbers.

Now turn the page to the September 2026 balance sheet, because a dramatic shift happened in just six months between March 2026 and September 2026. Look at two lines side by side: Borrowings jumped nearly fivefold from ₹72 crore to ₹352 crore, and Fixed Assets more than doubled from ₹253 crore to ₹518 crore while Capital Work-in-Progress shifted from ₹91 crore to ₹63 crore. At the same time, Other Assets—mostly receivables and inventory—climbed from ₹470 crore to ₹606 crore, and quarterly interest expense stepped up from ₹1–2 crore to ₹6 crore in Q2 FY27.

Why did debt surge by ₹280 crore in half a year? Management's Q2 FY27 disclosures explain the mechanics clearly. First, SEDEMAC is funding two major physical expansions—equipping the 120,000-square-foot MF3 plant in Chakan and acquiring 13 acres for MF5 in Tamil Nadu—through internal accruals, lease commitments, and debt rather than diluting shareholders. Second, working capital nearly doubled from ₹135 crore in March 2026 to ₹258 crore in September 2026 because tight global semiconductor lead times forced SEDEMAC to build chip inventory while paying suppliers faster to secure allocations.

That explanation makes operational sense, yet a disciplined analyst still flags three forensic checks. First, Free Cash Flow in FY26 was negative ₹47 crore—₹128 crore of operating cash flow minus ₹175 crore of capex—and H1 FY27 clearly consumed even more cash. Second, Debtor Days stretched from 24 days in FY25 to 46.1 days in FY26, reminding us that giant OEM customers dictate payment terms. Third, with ₹63–91 crore sitting in CWIP and automated screens flagging potential interest capitalization, you must verify in the annual footnotes how much borrowing cost is being capitalized onto the balance sheet rather than expensed on the P&L. Debt at ₹352 crore against ~₹246 crore of TTM EBITDA is still manageable at roughly 1.4x—provided MF3 ramps smoothly and cash conversion turns positive in FY28.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The September 2026 balance sheet marks SEDEMAC's transition from an asset-light, self-funding R&D scale-up into a heavy-capex, debt-assisted manufacturing expansion. A 1.4x debt-to-TTM-EBITDA ratio is not alarming on its own, but it removes the margin of safety if semiconductor inflation or OEM demand hiccups hit simultaneously.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing Cash Conversion and Interest Capitalization
paragraphs: Let us run one more forensic check on SEDEMAC's cash-conversion cycle so nothing surprises you in future filings. Between FY23 and FY25, SEDEMAC looked almost self-funding: pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA conversion ran at 166% in FY23, 85% in FY24, and 87% in FY25, and borrowings fell from ₹170 crore in FY24 to ₹64 crore in FY25. In FY26, however, pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA stepped down to 71% (₹128 crore of CFO on ₹217 crore of EBITDA) as Debtor Days stretched from 24 to 46.1 days, even though Days Payable temporarily ballooned from 76 to 128 days to cushion the working-capital hit.

Then came H1 FY27, when semiconductor tightness forced SEDEMAC to reverse that payable cushion—paying chip suppliers faster while simultaneously funding MF3 and MF5. That double squeeze is why working capital jumped from ₹135 crore to ₹258 crore and borrowings leaped to ₹352 crore. Over the next four quarters, watch two ratios like a hawk: first, whether Q2 FY27's ₹6 crore quarterly interest run-rate stays contained or climbs alongside Ind AS 23 capitalized interest on CWIP; and second, whether Free Cash Flow swings back into positive territory once MF3 commercial production scales and capex intensity tapers.
